home_content_block_body:
Gardens in Southampton vary widely. Compact terraced plots sit near the waterfront, while the leafier northern suburbs hold large family gardens on generous plots. Most landscaping work here calls for a different approach in each setting.

In Bassett Heath, the large detached houses on roads like Saxholm Way and Pinehurst Road tend to come with long, mature plots. Tree roots, changes in level and established planting shape what can go where. Layouts like these need careful thinking before any hard landscaping or new planting begins. Portswood's conservation area houses were built mostly in the early twentieth century on generous frontages. Paving and fencing work there carries extra weight. The front garden layout falls under Article 4 controls that limit what can be changed without permission.

For regular upkeep, our [gardener](/gardener/) work covers lawn mowing, hedge trimming, weed control and mulching. Bigger changes to a garden's shape or layout go through our [landscape gardener](/landscape-gardener/) service. That takes on new lawns, paving and walling, garden makeovers and planting. Where a project needs a drawn plan before work begins, our [landscape designer](/landscape-designer/) covers design and build from concept through to completion. Turf care and lawn renovation sit under our [lawn care service](/lawn-care-service/), which covers seeding, turf laying and ongoing maintenance.

We cover [landscaping in Romsey](/locations/romsey/), [landscaping in Winchester](/locations/winchester/), and [landscaping in Eastleigh](/locations/eastleigh/), as well as the villages and towns in between.

Call [CV: phone] to talk through what your garden needs.

Get that foundation wrong and a paved surface will sink or hold water within a few winters, however good it looks when first laid.

faq_answer (How much does landscaping cost in Southampton?):
It depends on the scope of the work. Regular maintenance is priced differently from a full garden redesign, a new patio or hard landscaping with groundwork. In Southampton, access and ground conditions can also affect the price. We visit first and give you a fixed price before anything is agreed, so there are no surprises once work begins.

faq_answer (Is it better to lay turf or sow grass seed?):
Turf gives you a usable lawn sooner; seed costs less and suits larger areas. Both take longer to establish when the ground is not prepared first. In Southampton, compacted or waterlogged soil will hold back either option through the first growing season, so the condition of the ground often matters as much as the choice between the two.

faq_answer (What happens if something isn't right after the job?):
If something isn't right after the job, let us know. Every trade works to a standard of reasonable care and skill, and we take that seriously. Raising it directly with us is the quickest way to get it looked at. We're here to make sure the finished work is what was agreed.

faq_answer (How long does a garden landscaping project take?):
It depends on the scale, the groundwork involved and the materials chosen. A straightforward fencing run or new patio is a shorter job than a full garden makeover with levelling, new lawns and planting. Hard landscaping days can also be moved by wet weather, since working on saturated ground undermines the finished result. We discuss the expected timeline when we visit.

faq_answer (Why does water sit on my patio or lawn after rain?):
Usually one of three things. The ground drains slowly, the surface falls the wrong way so water pools rather than runs off, or there's no route for water to escape once it collects. Near Southampton's rivers and coast, ground can hold water seasonally well after rain stops. Working out which cause applies matters, because each one has a different fix.
